definition: A model in which all parameters are used for every input, as opposed to sparse architectures that activate only a subset.
details: Most traditional transformer language models are dense, meaning the full network is engaged for every token processed, which becomes increasingly costly to run as model size grows.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. That blueprint is Dense Model.
